title: Galaxy ESO 137-001: Visible (Hubble)
caption: The jellyfish galaxy ESO 137-001, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: ESO 137-001 · constellation Triangulum Australe · about 220 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Left of center, a white-and-blue swirl trails blue filaments downward, its translucent white arms winding clockwise. This is ESO 137-001, a spiral galaxy about 220 million light-years away in the constellation Triangulum Australe, seen by Hubble in visible light. Astronomers call it a jellyfish galaxy because ribbons of young blue stars hang from its disk like tentacles.

The galaxy belongs to a cluster called Abell 3627. Hot, thin gas fills the space between a cluster's galaxies and acts like a headwind on any galaxy moving through it. That wind strips away gas and dust in a process called ram pressure stripping. Since galaxies need gas to make stars, stripping can bring star formation to an early end.

In X-rays, ESO 137-001 trails a giant tail of hot gas that stretches across 260,000 light-years, almost three times the galaxy's width. Stars seem to be forming in that tail, which puzzles researchers because stripping should have heated the gas. When the image was released in 2019, a team planned to study the tail with Webb's Mid-Infrared Instrument once the telescope launched.

understand.summary: A Hubble Space Telescope image in visible light. NASA has not published the filters or color mapping for this image.
understand.eye: Hubble's visible-light view shows the blue streamers of young stars, but the giant tail of hot gas only appears in X-ray light, which the eye cannot see.

explore: ESO 137-001 is roughly as big as the Milky Way, with slightly less mass. Researchers planned to target star formation close to the galaxy, in the middle of the tail and near its end. Because material at the far end was stripped first, comparing these sites could show how the process changed over time.
sources: NASA release: A “Jellyfish” Galaxy Swims Into View of NASA’s Upcoming Webb Telescope
alt: A white-and-blue spiral galaxy left of center with several blue filaments trailing downward from it.
